title: Metal-Organic Cage Synthesis Process
description: A comprehensive schema for defining the synthesis process of Metal-Organic Cages (MOCs), including identity, synthesis conditions, characterization, properties, and applications. This schema incorporates insights from adaptive tetrahedral cages with phosphorus functionalities and expert feedback for improved structure and clarity.

cage_identity.description: Identity and structural information about the MOC, including composition, topology, and isomerism.

name.description: The name of the MOC, often denoted as '[MxLy]n[counter_ion]-n' or a shorthand.

formula.description: The chemical formula of the MOC, including metal ions, ligands, and counter ions.

composition.description: The composition of the MOC, including metal centers and ligands.

metal_centers.description: The metal centers used in the MOC, including their types, oxidation states, and absolute ratios.

type.description: The type of metal ion (e.g., Zn, Co, Cu, Rh, Fe).

oxidation_state.description: The oxidation state of the metal ion.

absolute_ratio.description: The absolute stoichiometric ratio of the metal ion in the MOC.

ligands.description: The ligands used in the MOC, including their names, synthesis methods, and absolute ratios.

name.description: The name or formula of the ligand.

synthesis_method.description: The synthesis method used for the ligand, e.g., 'imine condensation', 'Sonogashira-type coupling'.

absolute_ratio.description: The absolute stoichiometric ratio of the ligand in the MOC.

name.description: The chemical name or formula of the ligand source.

source_type.description: Whether the source is commercially available or synthesized.

quantity.description: The amount of ligand source used, typically in millimoles (mmol) or moles (mol).

counter_ions.description: The counter ions used for charge balancing.

name.description: The name or formula of the counter ion.

absolute_ratio.description: The absolute stoichiometric ratio of the counter ion in the MOC.

topology.description: The geometric and structural topology of the MOC.
